RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generative Adversarial Networks) combines parametric memory and non-parametric memory in the following way:

RAG models use a retriever component that retrieves text documents (parametric memory) and uses them as additional context when generating the target sequence (non-parametric memory). This means that the model first retrieves relevant information from text documents, and then uses this information as additional context to generate the target sequence.

In other words, RAG models leverage both parametric (text-based) and non-parametric (contextual) memory to improve their performance on sequence-to-sequence tasks, such as question answering (QA).
